note: Mock mode lines (no AI). 15 per tactic. {country} = the delegate's country, {student_country}, {topic}, {quote} = a few of the student's own words.

interrupts.text: Point of information! Does the delegate of {student_country} have a plan for {topic}, or just a feeling?
Sorry to cut in, delegate. You said '{quote}'. Who exactly does that help?
Point of information! How long would that take?
Will the delegate yield to a quick question? What happens if nobody agrees?
Hold on. Before you go on, which countries are already on board?
Point of information. Is that a promise or a hope?
Quick question, delegate. Who pays for that?
I must interrupt. That plan skips the hardest part of {topic}.
Point of information! Can the delegate name one example?
Excuse me, delegate. You keep saying '{quote}'. What does that mean in practice?
Point of information! {country} has tried that. It didn't work. Why would it now?
One second. Is the delegate aware this affects millions of people?
Point of information! What's your first step, exactly?
I'll jump in here. That sounds nice, but how do you measure success?
Point of information! Will {student_country} put money behind that?

demands_evidence.text: Source, delegate? Where does that come from?
That's a big claim. What evidence supports it?
{country} would love to see the data behind that.
Is that a fact, or a feeling? Show me the proof.
I need more than a guess. Do you have a number or an example?
Interesting. Can you name one study, one country, or one year?
Evidence, please. {topic} is too important for guesses.
That's an estimate at best. Where did you get it?
Without a source, that point doesn't stand. Try again?
I hear a claim. I don't hear proof. Which is it?
Can the delegate back that up with something real?
{country} works with facts. What facts do you have?
Prove it, delegate. One example will do.

rapid_stats.text: About a third of countries already tried that. Most gave up within five years.
Numbers matter, delegate. Costs go up about ten percent every year on {topic}.
Roughly half of the plans like yours never get funded. Why is yours different?
{country} spends a large share of its budget on this already. You want more?
Studies show progress is slow, maybe a few percent a year. Your plan promises magic.
Millions of people are affected by {topic}. Your plan reaches how many?
Most experts say it takes ten years or more. You said '{quote}'. Faster? How?
Two out of three similar programs went over budget. Do you have a fix?
The trend is clear and it's going the wrong way. What's your number?
Every year we wait, the cost grows. By how much does your plan cut it?
Nearly every region reports the same problem. A local fix won't do.
Quick math, delegate: more people, same money, same problem.
That's one example. The big picture says something else.
Statistically, your idea is a long shot. Convince me otherwise.

thought_experiments.text: Imagine every country did exactly what you said tomorrow. What breaks first?
Picture a small town with one factory. Your plan arrives. Who loses their job?
Imagine you're on a very fast train, delegate. Is your plan the brakes or the engine?
Suppose {country} says no. Does your plan still work?
Imagine it's ten years from now. Is {topic} solved, or just moved somewhere else?
Here's a puzzle: if everyone agrees but nobody pays, what happens?
Picture two neighbors arguing over one river. Your plan picks a side. Which one?
Imagine your plan works too well. What's the side effect?
Let's flip it. What if {student_country} was the country being asked to change?
Imagine a student your age in {country}. How does your plan change their day?
Suppose the money runs out halfway. Then what?
Picture a map with no borders. Now put them back. Does your plan survive?
Imagine a world where we do nothing. Is that really worse than your plan?
Relatively speaking, delegate, what if the problem is the solution?
Imagine you had one sentence to convince the whole room. Is '{quote}' it?

rhetorical_questions.text: Do we really think one resolution fixes {topic}?
Who here believes that plan pays for itself?
Is the delegate seriously asking {country} to carry the cost?
Haven't we heard this idea before?
And who checks that it actually happens? Nobody?
Can we honestly call that a solution?
You said '{quote}'. Isn't that exactly the problem?
Would any country sign that today? I don't think so.
Is it fair to ask the poorest countries to move first?
What could possibly go wrong? Everything, delegate.
Isn't it convenient that {student_country} pays the least?
Do we fix a leak by repainting the boat?
Should we really trust a plan with no timeline?
Who wouldn't want that? The people paying for it.
Are we solving {topic}, or just talking about it?

slippery_slope.text: If we accept that, next year it's twice as big. Where does it stop?
Today it's a small fee. Tomorrow it's a tax on everything.
Your plan opens a door, delegate. Who walks through it next?
Once one country does this, everyone will demand the same deal.
First the rules, then the fines, then the bans. {country} sees where this leads.
You said '{quote}'. That's how big problems start.
If we bend the rules for {topic}, what rule is safe?
Give one group an exception and soon everyone wants one.
This starts small, but small things grow.
Step by step, this ends somewhere nobody voted for.
Today it's voluntary. In five years it's mandatory. Admit it.
{country} has watched plans like this grow out of control.
If we allow that, what stops the next country from going further?
Every big mistake started as a reasonable idea, delegate.
Where's the line, delegate? Draw it for me.

emotional_appeal.text: Think of a family in {country} who depends on this. Your plan forgets them.
Behind every number is a person. Who speaks for them in your plan?
A child in a village doesn't care about committees. They care about today.
I've heard stories from {country} that would change your mind.
This isn't just policy, delegate. It's people's homes.
You said '{quote}'. Would you say that to someone who lost their job?
Imagine explaining your plan to a worried parent.
People are waiting for help, not speeches.
{topic} isn't abstract for the people living it.
Every day of delay is another family waiting.
Our citizens deserve a plan that feels like help, not homework.
Real people, real lives. Does your plan see them?
I'm thinking of the young people in {country}. Are you?
Hope matters, delegate. Your plan sounds like paperwork.
Let's not forget who this room is supposed to serve.

history_appeal.text: History shows plans like this fade after the first year.
We've been here before, delegate. It ended badly.
History shows that rushing {topic} creates new problems.
{country} remembers the last time someone promised a quick fix.
The past is full of resolutions that sounded like yours.
History doesn't repeat, but it rhymes. Your plan rhymes with failure.
Look back twenty years. What changed? Not much.
History shows trust is built slowly. Your plan skips that.
Every era thinks it found the answer. Most were wrong.
Past agreements on this worked only with strong checks. Where are yours?
History shows the small countries pay first. Not this time.
The record is clear, delegate, and it's not on your side.
Older plans failed for one reason: no follow-through. Same here?
History rewards patience. Your plan is in a hurry.

cites_treaties.text: Past UN resolutions already cover this. Why write a new one?
{country} signed earlier agreements on {topic}. Your plan ignores them.
There are treaties for this. Does your plan respect them?
The UN Charter talks about cooperation, not pressure.
Earlier resolutions asked for voluntary steps. You want rules. Why?
International law is clear about sovereignty, delegate.
You said '{quote}'. Which treaty supports that?
Agreements only work if countries sign them. Who signs yours?
The last agreement on this took years to negotiate. Yours took one sentence.
{country} follows the agreements it signed. Will {student_country}?
We already have frameworks. Use them before inventing new ones.
Past resolutions failed because they had no money attached. Does yours?
A treaty without checks is just a wish.
Let's build on what the UN already agreed, not start over.
Your plan conflicts with earlier commitments. Which one wins?

reframes_question.text: The real question isn't {topic}. It's who decides.
You're asking how. I'm asking why.
Let's be honest: this is really about money.
You said '{quote}'. But that's not the question that matters.
This debate isn't about rules. It's about trust.
Maybe the question is whether this belongs at the UN at all.
You framed it as a problem. {country} sees an opportunity.
Let's zoom out. Is {topic} a cause or a symptom?
The question isn't whether to act. It's who goes first.
This isn't about what's right. It's about what works.
Let me ask a better question: who benefits?
The issue isn't speed. It's fairness.
Let's call it what it is: a question of power.
The real debate is about who pays and who gains.

turns_point_around.text: You said '{quote}'. Exactly. That's why {country} disagrees.
Thank you, delegate. You just made my argument.
If that's true, then your own plan fails the same test.
You're worried about cost? So is {country}. That's why we oppose you.
By your logic, {student_country} should go first.
Your example proves my point, not yours.
You want fairness? Then let's apply it to your plan too.
If people matter most, why does your plan ask them to wait?
You said it yourself: it's hard. So why rush?
Interesting. That reason is exactly why this won't work.
Your best point is also your biggest problem.
I agree with your facts. I disagree with your conclusion.
If we follow your idea all the way, {country} wins the argument.
You named the risk. Your plan doesn't fix it.
Thank you for that. It shows why we need a different plan.

yes_no_traps.text: Yes or no, delegate: will {student_country} pay for this?
Simple question. Yes or no: does your plan have a deadline?
Yes or no: would {student_country} accept the same rules?
You said '{quote}'. Yes or no, is that a promise?
Yes or no: can you guarantee it works?
One word, delegate. Will it cost jobs? Yes or no?
Yes or no: is there a backup plan?
Do you support punishing countries that don't follow it? Yes or no?
Yes or no: have you asked the countries most affected?
Just yes or no. Is your plan voluntary?
Yes or no: would you vote for this if {country} wrote it?
A simple yes or no: is the money already found?
Yes or no: does your plan help {country}?
Yes or no, delegate. Is this realistic?
I'll make it easy. Yes or no: do you trust the numbers?

pins_down_dodges.text: With respect, that wasn't my question. Who pays?
You didn't answer. I'll ask again: how does it work?
That's a nice speech, delegate. It's not an answer.
You said '{quote}'. That avoids the question. Try again?
Let's be precise. What exactly is your first step?
I'll wait for a real answer.
Answer the question, please. Then we can move on.
Still waiting, delegate. When does it start?
That's a different question. Answer mine first.
Clear and simple, please. Yes, no, or how?
I asked about cost. You talked about values. Which is it?
Let me ask again, slowly: what's the plan?
You're dodging, delegate. Politely, but dodging.
One clear answer, and I'll stop asking.

procedural_objections.text: Point of order! The delegate will refer to other delegates in the third person.
Point of order. The delegate should address the chair, not me directly.
Is the delegate aware of the rules on speaking time?
Point of order: please use formal language in committee.
The delegate of {country} notes that was not a question to the chair.
Point of order! That remark is off topic.
Procedurally, delegate, you need a motion for that.
Point of order: the delegate said 'you.' The correct form is 'the delegate.'
Is that a motion or an opinion, delegate?
The rules say one point at a time. Which is yours?
Point of order. Please stay on {topic}.
The delegate of {country} requests that speakers follow procedure.
Point of parliamentary inquiry: does the delegate yield the floor?
That would require a two-thirds vote, delegate.
Point of order! The chair did not recognize that point.

long_answers.text: Let me explain why, step by step. First the cost, then the timing, then who carries it. On all three, {country} disagrees.
There are many sides to {topic}, delegate, and your plan covers only one of them. We must think about money, people, and time together.
To answer properly, I need to start at the beginning: this problem is old, it is complicated, and it won't be fixed in one vote.
You said '{quote}', and I want to unpack that carefully, because it hides three different problems inside one sentence.
Allow me to walk through the full picture. Your plan is a start. But a start is not a plan, and a plan is not a result.
{country} has thought about this for a long time. There is history, there is cost, and there is trust. Your plan skips two of the three.
First, the money isn't there. Second, the deadlines are vague. Third, nobody checks. Fourth... well, I'll stop at three.
This is a long story, delegate, and your plan reads only the last page.
Let me be thorough. Who pays, who checks, who benefits, and who gets left out? Your plan answers one.
There's the short answer and the long answer. The long answer is: it depends on things your plan ignores.
To be complete: the idea is kind, the timing is wrong, the funding is missing, and the support is thin.
I could talk about this all day. Briefly: {country} needs more detail before it agrees to anything.
Every country in this room sees {topic} differently. A good plan has to work for all of them, not just {student_country}.
Consider the whole chain: decision, money, action, results. Your plan breaks at the second link.
Let me take my time on this, because it matters: rushed plans make new problems.

changes_subject.text: Before we go further, let's talk about the real issue: funding.
That's one angle. But what about trade? That's where {country} is strong.
Interesting. But the bigger problem is education. Let's start there.
Let's move on to something more urgent: who enforces this?
You keep talking about '{quote}'. {country} wants to talk about results.
Let's focus on the countries that are already doing well instead.
Fine. But nobody has mentioned technology yet. Let's.
We could debate that forever. Let's talk about jobs instead.
Let's step back to the part your plan forgot: the timeline.
A better topic: what is {student_country} doing at home?
Before that, let's look at the data, not the hopes.
I'd rather discuss solutions that already work.
That's a side issue. The main issue is trust.
Let's talk about what {country} has already done.
Moving on: the real fight is over the budget.

flattery_then_attack.text: What a lovely point, delegate. However, it falls apart on cost.
You speak beautifully. Sadly, the plan doesn't match the speech.
I truly admire your passion. I don't admire your numbers.
You said '{quote}'. Wonderful words! Empty plan.
{student_country} always brings great ideas. This isn't one of them.
Brilliant start, delegate. Now let's look at the hole in the middle.
I agree with your heart. I disagree with your homework.
Such a thoughtful delegate. Such a thin proposal.
Thank you for that excellent speech. Now, the problems.
Very clever. Too clever. It won't survive a vote.
You clearly prepared. Did you prepare for the cost question?
Kind words, delegate. Let me be less kind about the plan.
Lovely idea. Who pays for lovely?
I'm impressed. Not convinced, but impressed.
You're a strong speaker. That's why I expected a stronger plan.

devils_advocate.text: Let me argue the other side: maybe doing nothing is safer.
What if {topic} isn't a problem at all? Prove it is.
Playing devil's advocate: why should {country} care?
Suppose your plan is wrong. What's the cost of being wrong?
Here's the opposite view: the market will fix this on its own.
You said '{quote}'. What if the opposite is true?
Let me test you. Why not let each country decide alone?
Some say this is none of the UN's business. Answer them.
Argue against yourself for a second. Where's the weak spot?
What if the people affected don't want your help?
Maybe slower is better. Convince me it isn't.
Here's a hard one: why should rich countries pay more?
Let's say I agree. Now tell me why someone smart would disagree.
What if your plan helps one problem and causes two?
I'll take the unpopular side: this can wait. Change my mind.

finds_contradictions.text: Earlier you said it would be cheap. Now it needs a fund. Which is it?
You said '{quote}'. That doesn't match what you said before.
A minute ago it was voluntary. Now it's required?
Interesting. Your first point and your last point disagree.
Earlier you said speed mattered. Now you want five years?
You said every country is equal, then asked {country} to pay more.
Wait. You said nobody would lose jobs. Now there's job training?
Which version of your plan should we vote on?
You keep changing the story. {country} prefers one story.
First it was simple. Now it's complicated. Which is true?
You agreed with me earlier. Why the change?
I wrote down your words. They don't line up.
That's the opposite of your last answer, delegate.
Let's pick one position and test it. Which one?

analogies.text: Your plan is like fixing a roof during a storm. Brave, but wet.
That's like buying shoes without knowing the size.
{topic} is a puzzle. You're forcing one piece into the wrong spot.
It's like planting a tree and digging it up every week to check the roots.
Your plan is a bike with one wheel. It might move, but not far.
This is like a group project where only one person works.
You said '{quote}'. That's like promising a cake with no flour.
Think of it like a bridge. Your plan builds one side.
It's like putting a bandage on a broken leg.
Your plan is a map without roads.
It's like a recipe that says 'add stuff.' How much stuff?
This debate is a relay race, and you dropped the baton at cost.
That's like turning up the music to ignore a smoke alarm.
Like a lighthouse with no light, delegate. Pretty, but not helpful.
It's like a team with no coach. Who's in charge?

demands_specifics.text: Which country? Which year? Be specific, delegate.
How much money? Give me a number.
When, exactly? This year? In ten years?
Who runs it? Name the agency.
Which part of {topic} does this fix first?
Specifics, please. Where does it start?
How many people does it help? Roughly?
Which countries have agreed so far?
What does success look like, in one number?
Name one place where this already works.
Who checks the results? Which group?
Be precise. What changes on day one?

quotes_you_back.text: You said, and I quote, '{quote}'. Do you stand by that?
Let me read that back: '{quote}.' Is that really the plan?
You just said '{quote}.' {country} would like you to explain.
'{quote}' — that's a big promise. Can you keep it?
Your exact words were '{quote}.' Let's test them.
Interesting... '{quote}.' What did you mean by that?
I'll quote you: '{quote}.' Now, who pays?
'{quote}.' I'll remember that when we vote.
You said '{quote}.' Earlier, you said something different.
Hold on. '{quote}.' Is that a fact or an opinion?
I'm reading my notes: '{quote}.' Explain, please.

so_what.text: So what? Why does that matter to {country}?
So what changes for real people?
And that leads to what, delegate?
So what if it's popular? Does it work?
Why is that important right now?
You've told me what. Tell me why.
Interesting fact. Why should the room care?
That's a detail. Where's the big picture?
I'm listening. Why does it matter?

side_deals.text: Let's make a deal. {country} supports you if you support our trade clause.
I could vote yes... if {student_country} helps with our funding.
Here's an offer: we sign, you add our amendment.
{country} has friends in this room. Want them on your side?
A trade, delegate: your timeline for our exception.
You said '{quote}'. We'd agree, for a price.
What's {student_country} willing to give to get our vote?
Let's talk privately after this. I think we can work something out.
Support our bloc on the next topic, and we'll support you on this one.
Every vote has a cost. What's yours?
We could co-sponsor this. With a few small changes.
I'll bring three countries with me if you drop the deadline.
Give a little, get a lot. That's how this room works.
Add our name as a sponsor and we'll talk.

veto_threat.text: Careful, delegate. That plan won't survive the Security Council.
A veto is on the table if you keep that clause.
You said '{quote}'. {country} cannot accept that. We would block it.
Rewrite it, or {country} votes no in the place that counts.
We have the power to stop this. Give us a reason not to.
That clause is a red line for {country}.
You'll need {country} on board. Right now, you don't have us.
We've blocked plans like this before.
Count the votes, delegate. Then count the vetoes.
A veto isn't a threat. It's a promise.
Change the enforcement part, or we stop it.
{country} will not be pushed. Rethink it.
The permanent members need to agree. We don't.

compromise_offers.text: What if we meet in the middle: a smaller fee, a longer timeline?
{country} could accept half of that. Would you?
Let's find a middle ground. Voluntary first, required later?
You said '{quote}'. We could support a softer version.
A pilot program in a few countries first? Then we expand.
We both want progress. Let's agree on step one.
Here's a compromise: you keep the goal, we pick the timeline.
What if rich countries pay more at first, then it evens out?
Let's both give a little. Deal?
{country} can work with that if we add a review in two years.
Maybe we split the cost by region?
I hear you. Can we start smaller?
A shared fund, shared rules, shared credit. Interested?
We're closer than it sounds, delegate.
Let's write it together, line by line.

time_pressure.text: We're running out of time, delegate. Get to the point.
Quickly, please. The clock is ticking.
Time is short. What's your one main idea?
You said '{quote}'. Faster, delegate. Then what?
Ten seconds of point, please, not thirty seconds of warm-up.
While we talk, {topic} gets worse. Speed up.
We have minutes, not hours. What's the plan?
Wrap it up, please. One sentence.
The vote is soon. Are you ready or not?
{country} has places to be. Your point?
Short and sharp, please. Time matters.
Hurry, delegate. What's the first step?

silent_treatment.text: ...I'm still waiting for the main point.
...I'll let that sit for a moment.

mirror.text: So you're saying {country} should pay for {student_country}'s idea?
Let me repeat that: you want everyone to change, except you.
You said '{quote}'. So, in other words, it's not ready yet?
If I heard you right, the plan is: hope it works.
So your plan is a good wish with a deadline?
You're saying it's urgent, but it can wait five years?
So, to be clear, it costs nothing and fixes everything?
In other words, someone else will figure out the details?
You're saying people will just agree. Interesting.
So the answer to a big problem is a small fee?
If I understand, the plan is to make a plan?
Let me say it back: trust us, it'll work.
So you want rules, but no one to check them?
You mean {student_country} gets credit and {country} gets the bill?

with_all_due_respect.text: With all due respect, delegate, that won't work.
With great respect, {country} sees it very differently.
I mean this kindly: the plan has a big hole.
With all due respect, '{quote}' isn't a solution.
Respectfully, the numbers don't add up.
With every respect to {student_country}, that's unrealistic.
I say this with respect: who pays?
With all due respect, we've tried that.
Respectfully, delegate, you skipped the hard part.
I respect the effort. I can't support the result.
With all due respect, the timeline is fantasy.
Respectfully, {country} needs more than good intentions.
With respect, that answer was a dodge.
All respect to you, delegate. None to that plan.

worst_case.text: Worst case: the money runs out and nothing changes.
Picture it failing. Who gets hurt first?
If this goes wrong, {country} pays for the cleanup.
You said '{quote}'. And if it backfires?
Worst case, your plan makes {topic} worse.
Imagine the headlines if this fails.
The worst case isn't unlikely, delegate. It's common.
If one big country quits, the whole plan collapses.
What if people stop trusting the UN because of this?
Worst case: years of work, zero results.
If it fails, who takes responsibility?
The worst case for {country} is jobs lost and nothing gained.
Plan for the storm, not the sunshine.
If the worst happens, is there a plan B?
I've seen the worst case before. It looks like this plan.

cost_focus.text: How much, delegate? A rough number is fine.
You said '{quote}'. Lovely. What's the price tag?
{country} can't afford promises. Who funds it?
Money doesn't grow on resolutions. Where does it come from?
Every plan has a bill. Who gets yours?
Does {student_country} pay its share, or just talk about it?
Who pays when it costs more than expected?
Poor countries can't carry this. Who helps them?
Your plan is free on paper. Nothing's free.
What gets cut so this can be funded?
Cost first, then I'll listen to the rest.

sovereignty_focus.text: You said '{quote}'. Who gave the UN that power?
Every country is different. One rule for all doesn't fit.
We will not be told how to run our country.
Respect our borders and our choices.
Help is welcome. Orders are not.
Who checks our progress? Our own government. Not outsiders.
Sovereignty isn't a detail. It's the foundation.
Your plan sends inspectors. We say no.
Let each nation choose its own path on {topic}.
A plan that ignores sovereignty won't get votes.
Our people elected our leaders, not this committee.

human_rights_focus.text: Does your plan protect human rights, or just budgets?
People's rights come first. Where are they in your plan?
You said '{quote}'. What about the right to safety?
Every person deserves dignity. How does your plan ensure it?
{country} won't sign anything that ignores human rights.
Who protects the most vulnerable in your plan?
Your plan talks about countries. I want to hear about people.
Does anyone lose a right because of this?
Children, refugees, workers. Name one group your plan protects.
Human rights are the test. Your plan hasn't passed it yet.
Freedom of speech, privacy, safety. Which one does this help?
We need guarantees, not hopes, for people's rights.
A good plan protects people even when it's inconvenient.
Start with rights, then talk about rules.

security_focus.text: Is this safe? That's {country}'s first question.
What happens if bad actors use your plan?
You said '{quote}'. Is that a security risk?
Safety first, delegate. Then everything else.
Who protects the people running this program?
Your plan opens a door. Who else walks through it?
Security isn't a side issue on {topic}.
How do we stop this from being misused?
A plan that isn't secure isn't a plan.
What's the risk, and who manages it?
If something goes wrong, who responds?
Peace and safety come before speed.
We've seen good programs turned into weapons. How is yours protected?
Show me the safety plan, delegate.

outdated_data.text: Those figures are from years ago. Things changed.
You said '{quote}'. Is that still true today?
{country} has newer numbers. They say something else.
When was that measured? Last decade?
The world moved on. Your facts didn't.
That was true once. Is it true now?
Your source is out of date, delegate.
Update your numbers, then we'll talk.
Interesting history. What does today look like?
Things are moving fast. Your data isn't.
I'd check the date on that, delegate.

gentle.text: A fair point, delegate. Can you tell me a little more about how it works?
I see what you mean. What would be your first small step?
That's a good start. Who would it help the most?
Okay, delegate. {country} is curious. How would you pay for it?
Thank you. I like that idea. Is there one example you could share?

dodge.text: Hmm, I don't think that answered my question. Could you try again?
That was short, delegate. Can you say a bit more?
I'm not sure that was an answer. What's your main point?

evidence_ok.text: Hm. That's a real example. I'll give you that one, delegate.
A fair point, delegate. Your example helps. But is it enough?
